solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Spend little — pence on tough fabric (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one thing sitting on another comes after it, so P follows the fabric

blocks.note: scrim is a strong, coarse cotton or linen cloth

annotation.surface: A thrifty shopper weighs pennies against buying some hard-wearing cloth.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'Spend little' look like a comment on the pence; it is the definition. Scrim is the loosely woven cloth used in theatre and upholstery.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to scrimp is to economise hard, as in 'scrimp and save'.

entries.clue: So do be my madly significant person (8)

indicatorNotes.madly: something done madly is done wildly and without order, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: A lovesick plea: be mine, madly, my special someone.
annotation.walkthrough: The opening words look like broken grammar rather than raw letters, which hides the fodder in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, 'a somebody' means a person who matters, as in 'he thinks he's a somebody'.

entries.clue: Rubbish mostly ripped up (3)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of a word, but not all of it, so its last letter goes
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, a word turned up is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: reversal indicator for a down clue

annotation.surface: Junk that has been largely torn to pieces.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ripped up' reads as one phrase meaning shredded, but 'up' belongs to the wordplay and 'ripped' only supplies TORN; TOR written upwards gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Rot in the sense of nonsense, as in 'don't talk rot', is a plain synonym for rubbish.

entries.clue: Island people with island beachwear garment (7)

indicatorNotes.with: one thing with another is placed alongside it, so the pieces run on in order

annotation.surface: Islanders and their notorious swimwear.
annotation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea. The garment is the skimpy sling swimsuit made famous by the film Borat.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: this one-piece sling swimsuit for men is worn on the beach.

entries.clue: Whale’s smell attracting wolves round beach, every one going (8)

indicatorNotes.attracting: one piece draws the next to it, so they sit side by side
indicatorNotes.round: a word placed round another encloses it, as a fence goes round a field
indicatorNotes.going: letters that are going leave the word they sit in

blocks.note: hum = a bad smell, British slang

annotation.surface: A whale on the shore gives off a stink that draws wolves circling the beach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Every one' is EACH, and taking it out of BEACH leaves only its first letter, which PACK then goes round. Hum is British slang for a nasty smell.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the humpback, named for its arched back, is one species of baleen whale.

entries.clue: Civil servant short of confidence fairly regularly (14)

indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: short of = under, as in under budget
a confidence is a secret told in trust
the second, fourth and sixth letters of fAiRlY

annotation.surface: An official who is only moderately self-assured.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short of confidence' reads as one phrase about a timid official, but it breaks in two, and 'confidence' has its noun sense of a thing told privately.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an undersecretary is a senior official ranking below a secretary of state.

entries.clue: Verbal attack from European Marxists’ leader in charge (7)

indicatorNotes.leader: the leader goes in front of the rest, so a word's leader is its first letter

annotation.surface: A political tirade delivered by the head of a European communist party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marxists' leader' invites a name such as Lenin, but only the word's first letter is wanted, and 'European' is a nationality rather than an adjective for the Marxists.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a polemic is a forceful written or spoken attack on someone's views.

entries.clue: Large growth of transatlantic railroad supported by millions (8,3)

indicatorNotes.supported by: in a down clue what supports something sits underneath it, so M comes last

blocks.note: from a British view, transatlantic = American
the El, an elevated railroad in US cities such as Chicago

annotation.surface: A huge expansion of a railway across the Atlantic, funded by millions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large growth' suggests economic expansion to match the railroad and millions; it means something that grows, a big tree.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic stretch: a tree is something grown, and this North American species reaches thirty metres.

entries.clue: Equipment to bag up litter may include this (6)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, a word turned up is read from bottom to top

annotation.surface: Gear for bagging up rubbish, with which a pile of litter might be cleared.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Litter' suggests rubbish to be bagged, but it means a brood of young animals born together.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a cat's litter is its brood of young, so one member is included in it.

entries.clue: Style of writing they said could introduce it (8,6)

annotation.definition: Style of writing they said could introduce it

blocks.note: the surface suggests a literary style, but this is a grammatical form
'they said' is itself the kind of phrase that opens this form, as in 'they said it could'

annotation.surface: A remark that some rumoured phrase might start off a style of writing.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue demonstrates its own answer: 'they said could…' is how indirect speech is written, relaying words without quoting them.
annotation.definitionFit: Reported speech is the grammatical style for relaying what someone said, introduced by phrases such as 'they said'.

entries.clue: Popular film star is lead item, No.1 in play (7,4)

indicatorNotes.in play: letters put in play are set moving and rearranged

blocks.note: NO plus 1 as the letter I

annotation.surface: A star is the main attraction, the number one in the play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No.1' looks like 'number one' but gives NO and I, both part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a matinee idol is a handsome actor adored by audiences, a heart-throb of stage and screen.

entries.clue: Gobble up something vegan leaves unstarted (3)

indicatorNotes.unstarted: a word that has not been started is missing its first letter

blocks.note: what a vegan leaves off the plate

annotation.surface: A vegan leaves some food uneaten on the plate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads like greens a vegan might gobble; here it means leaves out, and the thing left out is MEAT, which loses its M.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to gobble something up is to eat it greedily.

entries.clue: Wrap the thing in a lot of earth (7)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another sits inside it
indicatorNotes.a lot of: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: BURROW (an animal's earth) without its last letter

annotation.surface: Instructions to bury something wrapped up in soil.
annotation.walkthrough: An earth is a fox's den, so a burrow. 'Wrap' looks like a verb opening the instructions; it is a noun for a food.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Mexican dish of filling rolled in a tortilla is sold as a wrap.

entries.clue: Freshly adapt and consider taking in east repeatedly (11)

indicatorNotes.taking in: a word taking something in holds it inside itself, as a coat is taken in

blocks.note: to rate = to consider, as in 'rated a genius'

annotation.surface: Advice to adapt afresh by looking eastward again and again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' asks for east twice, in two forms: the abbreviation E and ORIENT, the east itself.
annotation.definitionFit: The RE- prefix supplies 'freshly', and orientate means to adjust to surroundings.

entries.clue: Lettuce head eaten by deer (7)

indicatorNotes.eaten by: what is eaten ends up inside the eater

blocks.note: head = main, chief, as in head office
a roe is a small deer

annotation.surface: A deer munching a head of lettuce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a head of lettuce, which suits the surface, but it is the adjective meaning main.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: romaine, the American name for cos, is a variety of lettuce.

entries.clue: What returning space capsules can do is not much of a contribution (4,2,3,5)

annotation.definition: What returning space capsules can do

blocks.clueFragment: What returning space capsules can do
blocks.note: capsules coming back from space often splash down at sea
the idiom for an amount too small to matter

annotation.surface: A dry remark about space missions making little difference.
annotation.walkthrough: The first definition is literal: capsules parachute down into the sea. The second is the idiom for a negligible amount.
annotation.definitionFit: Capsules drop into the sea on splashdown; the idiom means a tiny amount set against what is needed.

entries.clue: Adolphe’s upset Lily (8)

indicatorNotes.upset: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters including the S

annotation.surface: Adolphe has upset a woman called Lily.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lily' has a capital so it passes as a woman's name; it is the flower.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the asphodel, the flower of the Greek underworld, belongs to the lily family.

entries.clue: Irregularity where son follows soldiers in red on manoeuvres (14)

indicatorNotes.follows: what follows comes after, so the S goes at the end
indicatorNotes.on manoeuvres: troops on manoeuvres move about, and so do these letters

annotation.surface: A son marches out of step behind redcoats on manoeuvres.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers in red' conjures redcoats, but it is simply thirteen letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a lack of order is an irregularity.

entries.clue: Sight’s best when mass is invisible around speed of light (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a possessive, standing in for the adjective 'of sight'

indicatorNotes.is invisible: a letter that is invisible cannot be seen, so it drops out
indicatorNotes.around: a word placed around another surrounds it on both sides

blocks.note: c is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light

annotation.surface: A physics note: vision is at its best where mass vanishes near light speed.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface borrows from relativity, so 'mass' and 'speed of light' seem to belong together; each is only a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective means 'of sight', so it fills the role of the possessive 'sight's'.

entries.clue: Old company head’s unfriendly attitude (7)

blocks.note: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British firm

annotation.surface: The former boss of a firm has a frosty manner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Company head' reads as the boss, but the two words split: ICI was a major British chemicals company, and a ness is a promontory, as in Dungeness.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: coldness of manner is the metaphorical ice in an unfriendly attitude.

entries.clue: Initially suspect more than one cleaner steals (6)

indicatorNotes.Initially: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken

annotation.surface: Suspicion that more than one cleaner is pilfering.
annotation.walkthrough: The cleaner looks like a person under suspicion; it is a cloth.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: to swipe something is to steal it.

entries.clue: Extreme point on board? Quickly move mine back (4,3)

indicatorNotes.back: a word sent back runs in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to wing = to fly or move fast

annotation.surface: A board-game tactic: rush your mine back from the edge of the board.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a game board, but it means aboard an aircraft; the question mark flags that the definition is playful.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: the outermost point of an aircraft, the vessel passengers are on board, is the end of a wing.

entries.clue: President Henry accepting current success (7)

indicatorNotes.accepting: a word accepting another takes it in, so the I goes inside

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
H = henry, the unit of inductance

annotation.surface: A president named Henry takes on a present-day triumph.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' seems to mean present-day; it is the physics symbol I. Henry is the SI unit of inductance, abbreviated H.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a triumph is a great victory or achievement.

entries.clue: Vegetable growing medium’s running short (3)

indicatorNotes.running short: a word running short falls one letter short, losing its end

blocks.note: peat is decayed plant matter used for growing plants

annotation.surface: A gardener finds the vegetable plot's compost is running low.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vegetable growing medium' reads as one phrase, compost for a veg patch; the first word breaks off as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the green seed of a climbing legume, eaten as a vegetable.

entries.clue: He declared a criminal rational (5-6)

indicatorNotes.criminal: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

annotation.surface: A man pronounced a criminal to be of sound mind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' sits as a noun in the courtroom surface; it is an adjective telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone clear-headed thinks sensibly and logically.

entries.clue: A factor in inherited nature (3)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits in the words that follow, across the gap between them

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and the first two of the second

annotation.surface: A reflection on what shapes inherited character.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the answer straddles the join of 'inherited nature' and is what carries that nature.
annotation.definitionFit: The &lit reads straight: DNA holds the genes, the factors that pass inherited traits on.

entries.clue: Wary about time tailing bird in covert (8)

indicatorNotes.about: a word about another goes round it
indicatorNotes.tailing: to tail is to follow behind, so T comes after the bird

blocks.note: shy = wary, as in 'fight shy of'
the teal is a small duck

annotation.surface: A cautious birdwatcher waits as time passes behind a bird in the undergrowth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covert' looks like a noun for a thicket where birds shelter, fitting the surface; it is the adjective meaning secret.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stealthy action is done covertly, to avoid notice.

entries.clue: Country ignoring former prime minister’s limitations (6)

indicatorNotes.ignoring: to ignore something is to leave it out
indicatorNotes.limitations: a word's limits are its boundaries, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the outer letters D and I, to be dropped

annotation.surface: A nation that brushes aside an ex-premier's shortcomings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Limitations' reads as his failings; it means his edges, and removing them leaves the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Middle Eastern state founded in 1948 is a country.
